clue.text: Song that's naughty — everyone joins in

indicators.note: joins in says the word for everyone enters the word for naughty

parts.note: naughty means bad
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A rude song gets the whole crowd singing along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' and 'everyone' read as a description of the song, but 'joins in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song, so it is a straightforward synonym.

parts.note: reads as overseeing something for a modest fee, but the small charge is a child in your care

explanation.definitionFit: Minding a little child, a small charge, while the parents are out is exactly this job.

clue.text: Very drunk, loses opening in game

indicators.note: loses opening says the first letter of the word for very drunk goes

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: A heavily drunk player stumbles at the start of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses opening' drops the B from BLOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo, so it is an example of a game.

indicators.note: Possibly hints that the letters given may be arranged another way

parts.note: the letters of a and Sûreté, accent ignored

explanation.surface: A question about whether the French police detective force is rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the letters of A SURETE; the Sûreté is the French detective police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and stiff both describe a severe, formal, unbending manner.

definitions.meaning: to agree or say yes to something
split as two words, '...' means when it has been posted

explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal agreement, and read as two words it means as sent through the post.

clue.text: Observe present and past in child's play

parts.note: observe in the present tense is see
the past tense of see is saw

explanation.surface: Watching the present and the past in a game of children.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb see is given in both tenses: present then past.
explanation.definitionFit: A see-saw is a playground plank children ride, literally a piece of child's play.

clue.text: Came up with a diet change for the undernourished

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters given

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone devised a new diet for starving people.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin from lack of food, the result of being undernourished.

indicators.note: around tells us the word built is turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Port facilities constructed around a rail line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the word built. Tilbury Docks are London's main port, on the Thames estuary in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilbury Docks are a major port on the Thames estuary, so the name stands for docks.

definitions.meaning: to put others first, setting aside one's own interests
to behave badly, forgetting one's manners

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to set aside self-interest and to let one's temper or manners slip.

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as does but

explanation.surface: Arranging to meet someone in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to meet or adjoin at a boundary, as neighbouring properties do.

clue.text: Plays the defensive type of cricket for which Derbyshire is noted?

definitions.text: Plays the defensive type of cricket
definitions.meaning: a batter who blocks every ball without trying to score
the Derbyshire Peak District is famous for its dry-stone field boundaries

explanation.definitionFit: A stonewalling batter blocks defensively; Derbyshire fields are bounded by drystone walls.

clue.text: Received a hero's treatment when landed

indicators.note: treatment says the letters given are worked over into a new order

parts.note: the letters of a and hero's, the S included

explanation.surface: Someone got a celebrity welcome on arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land, the state of someone who has landed from a ship.

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, like goodness me

explanation.definitionFit: Both words serve as exclamations of surprise, and the adjective means courteous and benevolent.

indicators.note: breaking says the words given are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: To be at liberty is to be free, not confined.

clue.text: There's no end of cats here

definitions.text: There's no end of cats here

parts.words: There's no end of cats here
parts.note: sounds like a place full of cats, but means one where the cats lack tails, their ends

explanation.definitionFit: The island in the Irish Sea is home to the Manx breed, famous for having no tail.

definitions.meaning: a prop or brace, as in a corset or a mast's rope

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to remain somewhere and a supporting strut or rope.

indicators.note: in places the student's letter within the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
L is the learner, student, from L-plates

explanation.surface: A thoughtful undergraduate punting on a university river.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside CAM, the river at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To be philosophical about setbacks is to stay composed and serene.

clue.text: Get it all together, but not in time to pass

indicators.note: to means the late piece is attached after the mountain pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
late means not in time

explanation.surface: Gathering everything but arriving too late to qualify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' signals that the second piece is joined on after the first; 'pass' is a mountain pass, not passing an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate is to gather and arrange materials into order.

clue.text: Where to see ships under repair or those undergoing trials

definitions.text: Where to see ships under repair
definitions.meaning: in a dry dock for maintenance
the defendant's enclosure in a criminal court

explanation.definitionFit: Ships are repaired in a dock, and defendants on trial stand in the court's dock.

parts.note: to hog is to keep to oneself
a wash, as taken in a bath

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of hogging the bathroom, and being told it's rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash is informal for nonsense, originally pig swill.

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a cow
a slip is a petticoat

explanation.surface: A tidy underskirt in pale yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy but is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild flower of the primrose genus.

parts.note: sounds like praise for a good-natured person, but refers to real ..., the old indoor court game

explanation.definitionFit: Real tennis is the original indoor version of the racket game, so this is literally real sport.

definitions.meaning: a bloomer is a long crusty loaf

explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are blunders, and a bloomer is also a kind of loaf a baker makes.

clue.text: Leave university party in appropriate attire

indicators.note: in puts the party within the attire

parts.note: academic dress at university is a gown
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Quitting college after a formal ball in proper dress.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, going down means leaving the university; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage to go down is to leave Oxford or Cambridge at term's end or for good.

clue.text: A number left on a trip for the pottery

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: on a trip suggests the word left is tripped up and jumbled

explanation.surface: Several people leave on holiday to visit a ceramics works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a trip' is the anagram signal for 'left'; Roman numerals give the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware named after the Dutch town.

clue.text: Fish woman a source of bad feeling

parts.note: a salmon is a fish
Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A fishwife who makes everyone feel unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmonella bacteria cause food poisoning, a source of feeling ill.

parts.note: reads as meaning merely a token, but describes the flower that symbolises purity

explanation.definitionFit: The white flower is a traditional emblem of purity, so it is symbolic of being pure.

indicators.note: another order says the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man joins a different religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so it is an example of a man.
The phrasal verb means both to confine someone and to make them be quiet.
